correctness.rationale: Let a>0, b∈R and μ be compact invariant. By the y-coordinate map and invariance, y#μ=(bx)#μ, so E[y]=bm and Var(y)=b²Var(x). By x-coordinate invariance, aE[x²]=1-(1-b)m. The roots x± of ar²+(1-b)r-1 have Δ=(1-b)²+4a>0; Vieta gives Var(x)=(x_+-m)(m-x_-). Nonnegativity forces m between roots. Thus the barycenter lies on y=bx between the fixed points, and the total variance (1+b²)Var(x) equals the Euclidean product of its distances to p±. Endpoint zero variance forces both x,y constant and μ a corresponding fixed-point atom; equal fixed-atom mixture attains the sharp L²/4 bound. Works also at b=0, b<0, |b|≥1 without needing invertibility. Independent exact fractions at a=7/5,b=3/10 gave Δ=609/100, max Var(x)=609/784 and max total variance=66381/78400. No attractor existence, covariance off-diagonal, or dynamical chaos is established; checker verifies only identities, not the invariant-measure premise.
